subject: Re: Medilane prepilot credit — ledger classification & invoice offset
messages:
From: Sara Patel <accounts@medilane.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Lewis <chris.lewis@medilane.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Pre-pilot credit approval and invoice treatment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the flexibility on the pre-pilot. Finance approved a $25,000 promotional allowance to cover the first 60 days of usage, which Chris and I agreed would be applied as a credit memo against the pilot invoice.

Quick question for your team: do you prefer we receive a credit memo that offsets the pilot invoice on posting (invoice netting), or would Redwood provide a pro-forma credit memo to be posted on our ledger and left as a contra-revenue item so our auditors can tie it to the pilot agreement? Our audit team (SF CPAs) prefers a clear contra-revenue trail, but we want to align with Redwood's standard practice.

Attached: Medilane_Credit_Approval_0427.pdf

—Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Finance, Medilane Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <accounts@medilane.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-pilot credit approval and invoice treatment

Sara — thanks for the note and the attachment. Congrats on getting internal sign-off.

High level: Redwood supports both approaches but we need to confirm the accounting entry that Medilane prefers. Options we typically surface: 
- Option A: Issue a credit memo that offsets the pilot invoice (invoice netting). This reduces the invoice amount when posted and is simple operationally.
- Option B: Issue a credit memo posted as a contra-revenue/allowance on Redwood's books so your auditors see a standalone credit memo record; the invoice remains historically intact and the credit is applied in accounting entries.

To route this correctly internally I'll loop in Finance and Revenue Ops. Marcus / Neha — can you confirm Redwood's preferred GLA mapping and whether there are reporting implications for a $25k promotional allowance? Also flag any limitations for customers in the US region.

Sara — if you have SF CPA contact details we can include them to ensure the format meets audit requirements.

Thanks,
—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pre-pilot credit approval and invoice treatment

Folks — three quick points from Finance: 
1) For $25,000 promotional allowances we prefer issuing a credit memo that posts to a contra-revenue account (Allowance for Promotional Credits) on our side and then applying it to the customer invoice for netting at month end. This produces the clean audit trail SF CPAs usually want while keeping AR reconciliations straightforward.
2) If Medilane insists on seeing a standalone pro-forma credit memo for their ledger, we can provide a PDF with the credit memo number and GL references, but the booking will still be contra-revenue on Redwood's books.
3) Please confirm the invoice number and desired posting date. We need that to produce the pro-forma and the system-generated credit memo.

Marcus — can you prepare a draft pro-forma credit memo (worksheet) with the GL mapping and bring to the thread? Vanessa — we'll need the signed approval doc in the file (Sara's PDF looks good) and the HubSpot deal id for cross-reference.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Financial Operations
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pre-pilot credit approval and invoice treatment

Attached is the draft pro-forma credit memo workbook (Proforma_Credit_Memo_0429.xlsx) and the suggested GLA mapping:
- Revenue GLA (gross): 4000-01
- Allowance for promotional credits (contra-revenue): 4000-99
- AR clearing: 1100-45

Notes: Posting as contra-revenue and applying the credit at invoice netting will produce the clearest audit trail and the smallest downstream impact to revenue recognition schedules. If Medilane requests a direct invoice offset with no contra line (i.e., never book the promotional allowance), we can do that operationally but Finance flags potential audit questions.

Requesting: 
- Stephanie: confirm the pilot invoice number (or expected invoice date).
- Sara / Medilane: confirm whether you want the credit applied on the pilot invoice posting date or as a month-end netting.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Analyst
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <accounts@medilane.com>, Chris Lewis <chris.lewis@medilane.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, SF CPAs <audit@sfcpas.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-pilot credit approval and invoice treatment

Sara / Chris — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Finance guidance (thread below) our recommended path is: 
1) Redwood will issue a system-generated credit memo for $25,000 that posts to our contra-revenue GLA.
2) We will provide Medilane with a pro-forma PDF (with credit memo number, GL references, and HubSpot deal id) so your auditors have the document to tie to your ledger.
3) The credit will be applied to the pilot invoice as an invoice netting entry on the posting date (please confirm if you prefer posting on 2027-05-01 or 2027-05-31).

Action items: 
- Sara: confirm preferred posting date.
- Vanessa: please open the credit memo in the billing system and attach the signed approval; cc the HubSpot link.
- Marcus / Neha: after posting please confirm the credit memo number and provide the pro-forma PDF to Medilane and SF CPAs.

Thanks — aiming to have the credit memo issued and the pro-forma to Medilane by EOD 2027-05-01 pending posting date confirmation.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
